testHarnessAssessment.verdict: NOT vacuous, but weaker than it looks — a re-model, not a test of the script
detail: 19/19 tests pass (11 + 8). Both files assert genuinely falsifiable properties: testPhase7FailsOnShortfallAgainstBaseline and test_zeroBaselineWouldBeVacuous_persistedBaselineIsNot both use vm.expectRevert against real state conditions, and testZeroBaselineWouldHaveBeenVacuous demonstrates the pre-fix bug explicitly. This is NOT the 'mock never fails => 0==0' pattern recorded in project memory.

HOWEVER: BptBaselinePersistence.t.sol tests a hand-transcribed contract `BptBaselineModel`, NOT script/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol. The file admits this ('if the script changes, this must be updated in lockstep'). I independently verified the transcription against the real source TODAY — :549, :564-572, :1725, :1729 match the model line for line — so the tests are currently faithful. Nothing enforces that they stay so.

VerifyPromotionReadyGuards.t.sol's source-level assertions are raw substring scans over the verifier's text. They are the ONLY structural link between the tests and the real file, and they are evadable in ways that matter: assertFalse(_contains(src,'OLD_POOLER')) would not catch a live-read fallback written through a local variable or a differently-named constant, and the cheatcode-literal scans ('startBroadcast','startPrank','vm.deal','vm.warp') do not catch a call to an INHERITED mutating helper such as _writeProgressFileWithStatus(...). See F-04.
Neither test file requires an RPC, which is why they ran in the headless story environment while the load-bearing :dry gate did not.

leadsResolution.detail: Source :96-98 checks only vm.envOr('PREVIEW_MODE', false). Its own NatSpec admits there is no cheatcode reporting the flag. leadsResolution.verdict: CONFIRMED, but fail-CLOSED by a downstream rail
leadsResolution.detail: resolveAddress() (scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js:98-106) regex-matches mainnet-addresses.ts and would happily return a 0x000…0 placeholder (the regex accepts any 40 hex chars). The snapshot JSON records `address` per staker, but _loadSnapshotUsers (script:1599-1601) reads ONLY .stakers.<key>.users and never cross-checks it against V1_STAKER_*. HOWEVER a wrong/incomplete user list is caught fail-closed at :1681 require(old.totalStaked() == 0, 'V1 still holds stake after migrate - widen the snapshot and re-run') and the conservation assert at :1682. The harm is therefore a LATE abort mid-broadcast on a one-shot Ledger run, not a silent bad migration. Filed as F-06, reconciling to L-07.
